What are the benefits of IPv6 on a website?

That you can use IPv6, i.e. the current IP protocol, and don't have to fall back to the old IPv4.

The IPv4 address space is only 232 (about 4 billion) addresses and is exhausted already. This is less a problem in the US and Europe, where address spaces have been given away generously. But it's a problem in the rest of the world. New Internet users cannot get an address and existing ones can't get more. Even if each human on earth only gets a single one, there aren't enough. IPv6 solves that by having 2128 addresses, so about one for each dust grain on the entire planet.

Most ISPs support both protocols (Dual Stack) nowadays, so they give you a single public IPv4 address and an IPv6 subnet (a pool of addresses). So if you have more than one device at home, which pretty much everyone has, you have to share the IPv4 address for all devices. They get local only addresses (i.e. not reachable via the internet), which will be translated into the single public one by the router (called NAT). This has been done forever, since IPv4 addresses have always been limited. Most people are used to that, but it creates problems with many protocols that rely on a direct device to device connection, like file transfer or VoIP. These protocols use complex mechanisms to work around the address translation. With IPv6 you get a whole subnet, usually 256 addresses. That's way more than there are IPv4 addresses at all, just for your home network. So each device can get its own public IP address and direct connections are no problem at all. There is also a feature called temporary addresses. So the devices pick a random address out of your address space to connect to servers to make it harder to track you.

There are also some ISPs (even European) already that switched to Dual Stack Lite, i.e. they only give you an IPv6 subnet but no public IPv4 address. IPv4 still works via a so called corporate grade NAT, that means you have to share a single address not only within your home network, but also with other customers of your ISP. That creates even more problems when using IPv4. Both technical and legal. If one user gets the IP blocked somewhere, many users are affected.

tl;dr: IPv4 is old, ran out of addresses, and has a ton of problems, so just use IPv6.
